newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FOCUS-RB warns NZ markets after conditions ease.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-RB warns NZ markets after conditions ease.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand on Friday issued its second warning in eight days to financial markets that monetary conditions were too loose.
Markets were not in a particularly receptive mood and only slowly allowed conditions to tighten by lifting 90-day bank bill rates and the New Zealand dollar.

The Monetary Conditions Index NZ/MCI gained 12 basis points in the first 40 minutes after the statement, leaving it 55 points easier than the Reserve Bank's desired level of 825 for the September quarter which it established in late June.
RB Governor Don Brash said in his statement that the bank had not changed its 50 point comfort zone either side of 825 but the market was reluctantly to move into that zone.
Economists said the bank was caught in a bind.
On the one hand it was grappling with conditions easier than it considers consistent with its 0-3 percent inflation target.
However, it would be most reluctant, and indeed unwise, to tighten conditions while the economy is in its current trough, they said.

One bond dealer was more blunt, saying "If that's the best they can do to try and jawbone conditions back to where they would like them, I think they are going to have a nasty shock at some point soon.
"I think the market might just take it to them and say 'If you guys think that conditions really should be tighter you have to do more about than just talk to us'," he added.

"It could almost come back as 'we dare you to tighten in this economic environment. How much do you trust your economic model?'," he said, adding he only expected a short-term impact from the latest statement.
On July 3 the Reserve Bank issued a first statement when the index fell to around 750 that conditions had easied too far and it wanted them closer to desired levels.

Since the bank's June policy statement, March quarter GDP showed the economy shrank 0.5 percent, worse than economists had forecast, while Friday's current account deficit was $4.5 billion in the March year, versus forecasts of $4.1 billion.
The New Zealand dollar fell sharply on the news while the TWI fell 25 basis points to a 10 month low of 65.69 helping take the MCI to a low of 748.57.
Economists expect further pressure on the currency which in turn would ease monetary conditions further.

"The current account deficit is 4.8 percent of GDP when the economy is brinking on a technical recession -- it is not the kind of dynamics that's I'd like to be managing," Citibank Australia's chief economist Stephen Koukoulas told Reuters Financial TV.
He agreed the RB was in danger of driving the economy into the ground. "It's certainly the case... They have crunched the economy pretty hard.
"The pace of demand is very, very weak -- now we have the current account problem coming through from arguably an overvalued currency," he said.
"It really suggests to us that monetary conditions in New Zealand should be eased quite dramatically," he said.
